newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC rises, Solidere falls on Beirut Stock Exchange. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BLC rises, Solidere falls on Beirut Stock Exchange. [CORRECTED 14:40 GMT]

text.p: Shares of Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose on higher turnover and Solidere shares fell on lower turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Friday.
BLC shares, continuing a strong performance since they listed on the exchange 12 days (Corrects from nine days) ago, rose to $12.25 from Thursday's $12.125 on trade of 22,500 shares against 10,000.
Also 12,500 BLC shares changed hands in a block trade at $12.125 inside the bourse hall, against 5,000 in two block trades on Thursday at $12.

BLC is the first commercial bank to list on the Beirut exchange since the market reopened a year ago. With the exception of one trading day this week, the shares have steadily risen from $11.25 on December 30 (Corrects from January 2) when they began trading.
Solidere A shares fell to $11 from Thursday's $11.125 and B shares also fell to $11.25 from $11.5.
Turnover in Solidere rose to 25,340 shares from 14,165 a day earlier and value was $282,020 from $159,715.625.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index fell 0.29 percent to 81.59 and the BLOM stock index also fell 1.35 percent to 933.11.
